label: Kayzen
terms_note: Kayzen self-serve DSP account; authentication token endpoint; rate limits not stated on the landing page. Free API (media spend via the DSP).

discovery.auth: token (POST authentication token with Kayzen account credentials / API key)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes** (Kayzen DSP REST API) Confidence: **high** — official developer hub read.

endpoints.call: POST /custom_audiences` · first-party audience API (audience API key)

reference.limits: - Rate limits not stated; free API; Kayzen terms.

fields.name: api_basic
fields.help: base64(<API_Key>:<API_Secret_Key>) — the Kayzen API key and secret (Kayzen UI > Account > API Key; 'Obtaining your Kayzen API key') joined by a colon and Base64-encoded, e.g. `printf '%s' 'KEY:SECRET' | base64`. Sent as `Authorization: Basic …` on POST /v1/authentication/token only.

fields.name: username
fields.help: Kayzen login email of the user the API key belongs to (token request body `username`).

fields.name: password
fields.help: Kayzen account password for that login (token request body `password`); the runtime exchanges it for a 30-minute bearer token and re-logs in on expiry or 401.

config_fields.name: advertiser_id
config_fields.help: Kayzen advertiser id used by `me` (GET /v1/balance?advertiser_id=…). Leave empty to use the API key's default advertiser.

me.note: GET /v1/balance → {advertiser: {balance, warning}}; there is no user endpoint, so the balance call verifies the token (and the optional configured advertiser).

list_campaigns.note: GET /v1/campaigns?advertiser_id=…&page=…&per_page=… (data[] + meta.total_entries). `account_id` is the Kayzen advertiser id (an enterprise admin switches advertisers with it). status is running / paused / …; `budget` is day_budget in USD (total_budget in raw). No status filter is documented, so `status` is not sent.

get_report.note: POST /v1/report_data {advertiser_id, start_date, end_date, metrics [impressions, clicks, advertiser_spend, ctr], group_by [day, campaign_id, campaign_name], filters {campaign_id: [id]} when campaign_id is given, per_page 1000, time_zone UTC} — synchronous 'Report Data' (no reusable report id). spend is advertiser_spend in USD.

update_budget.note: PATCH /v1/campaigns/{id} {data: {campaign: {day_budget}}} — day_budget is an integer number of US dollars (whole dollars only; a fractional amount is rejected before sending). This changes spend. A 422 `budget_overspend_risks` answer is returned as an error; the overspend warning is not bypassed. `currency` is ignored. Kayzen answers 200 with an empty object, so the result carries only status.

pause_resume.note: PUT /v1/campaigns/{id}/status {status: paused|running} (pause → paused, resume → running). Resuming restarts spend; a 422 `budget_overspend_risks` answer is returned as an error rather than bypassed.

not_offered.list_accounts: The API reference (https://developers.kayzen.io/reference) has no advertiser-listing endpoint; calls act on the API key's advertiser, and enterprise admins pass another 'Advertiser ID (for enterprise admin user)' explicitly (List Campaigns: 'The advertiser of the api key becomes the default advertiser. To switch advertisers, pass the advertiser id of that advertiser').

evidence: host api.kayzen.io: DNS ok, TLSv1.2 (GoDaddy.com, Inc.)
probe: 5/5 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 5/5 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
